glosses.notes: Can mean donating money, or the donated money itself.

examples.sentence: 学校一发消息，很多家长当天晚上就主动捐款，想先把最急着用的书和药买回来。
这次活动收到的捐款虽然不算特别大，但是对那几个家里突然有困难的人来说，已经非常重要了。
老人家里钱也不多，可是一听见有人生病没钱看病，他还是会先拿出一些钱来捐款。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the school sent out a message, many parents volunteered to donate money that same evening, hoping to buy back the books and medicine that were needed most urgently.
Although the donations received by this event were not especially large, they were already very important to those few families that had suddenly run into difficulty.
The old man does not have much money at home either, but as soon as he hears that someone is sick and cannot afford medical care, he will still first take out some money to donate.

glosses.notes: To donate money or objects, often in a formal or organized way.

examples.sentence: 图书馆后来收到一位老人捐赠的旧书，孩子一打开就看见里面还写着很多年前的名字。
公司决定把那批一直没用上的桌子和书全部捐赠给山里的学校，这样孩子上课时也能早点用上。
医生说，有人愿意长期捐赠这类药，对那些一直看病的人来说，真的能少很多不安。

example_translations.translation: The library later received old books donated by an elderly man, and as soon as the child opened one, he saw names written inside from many years ago.
The company decided to donate that batch of unused desks and books to a mountain school, so that the children there could start using them earlier in class.
The doctor said that if someone is willing to donate this kind of medicine over a long period, it can truly reduce a lot of anxiety for those who are always seeking treatment.

glosses.notes: Used for rolling or curling something up, or for something that rolls or curls into shape.

examples.sentence: 母亲把晒好的画慢慢卷起来以后，才放心放进盒子里，怕边上再折一下就不好看了。
风一大，门边那张纸一下被卷到脚边，孩子低头捡起来的时候，字已经有点看不清了。
父亲把长线轻轻卷在手上，怕一会儿出门时又像上次那样一下掉到地上。

example_translations.translation: After Mother slowly rolled up the dried painting, she only then felt at ease putting it into the box, afraid that if the edge bent one more time it would no longer look good.
As soon as the wind grew strong, the sheet of paper by the door was blown rolled over to their feet, and by the time the child bent down to pick it up, the writing was already a little hard to read.
Father lightly wound the long cord around his hand, afraid that when going out in a moment it would fall to the ground all at once the way it had last time.

glosses.notes: Used as a measure word for volumes of books, or as the noun volume in a book set.

examples.sentence: 这套书一共六卷，孩子刚看到第一卷的名字，就已经坐下来想先把后面的也一起找出来。
父亲年轻时最爱那一卷旧书，所以哪怕边上已经有些破了，他还是一直舍不得把它放远。
老师让我们先看第二卷，再回头看第一卷，这样很多前面不懂的地方反而会一下清楚起来。

example_translations.translation: This set of books has six volumes in all. As soon as the child saw the title of the first volume, he already sat down wanting to find the later ones too.
That old volume was Father's favorite when he was young, so even though the edges were already a little damaged, he still could not bear to put it far away.
The teacher told us to read the second volume first and then go back to the first, so that many places we had not understood earlier would instead suddenly become clear.

glosses.notes: Can mean the act of making a major decision, or the decision process itself.

examples.sentence: 这次决策不是一个人一下就定的，而是大家把能想到的问题都摆出来以后才慢慢决定的。
父亲常说，大人最难的不是做决策那一刻，而是做完以后还要一直把后面的事管下去。
公司后来换负责人时，第一件事就是让大家知道以后的决策到底由谁来定，不然开会总是乱。

example_translations.translation: This decision was not settled all at once by one person. Instead, everyone laid out every problem they could think of first, and only then was it slowly decided.
Father often says that the hardest thing for adults is not the moment of making a decision, but having to keep managing everything that comes afterward.
When the company later changed leadership, the first thing it did was make sure everyone knew who would be making decisions from then on, otherwise every meeting became chaotic.

glosses.notes: To lose hope completely or feel that there is no way out.

examples.sentence: 医生看他一直低着头，就先告诉他别太早绝望，因为现在还有好几种办法可以慢慢试。
她原来以为这件事已经没有路了，但是真到了最难的时候，反而比以前更不想让自己绝望。
老人常说，人一时看不见路很正常，可是只要还肯往前走，就别轻易绝望。

example_translations.translation: Seeing that he kept his head lowered, the doctor first told him not to despair too early, because there were still several ways they could try gradually.
She had originally thought there was no way forward in this matter, but when it truly reached the hardest moment, she instead became even more unwilling than before to let herself despair.
The old man often says that it is normal for a person to be unable to see the road for a while, but as long as one is still willing to keep walking forward, one should not despair lightly.

glosses.notes: An organized military force or army.

examples.sentence: 书里写到那支军队进城以前，路边已经站满了人，连最小的孩子都知道今天和以前不一样。
父亲年轻时常听老人讲那支军队是怎么走过来的，所以后来一直很爱听那段故事。
电影里的军队虽然走得很慢，但是大家都很安静，所以孩子看了以后一直没有说话。

example_translations.translation: The book described how before that army entered the city, the roadside was already full of people, and even the youngest children knew that this day was different from before.
When Father was young, he often listened to old people talk about how that army had made its way forward, so later he always loved hearing that part of the story.
Although the army in the film moved very slowly, everyone was very quiet, so the child kept silent for a long time after watching.

glosses.notes: A member of the armed forces; a soldier or servicemember.

examples.sentence: 站里那位老军人说话一直很慢，可是一提到年轻时一起走过来的朋友，眼里还是一下就有了很亮的光。
孩子第一次近看穿着整齐衣服的军人时，连平时最爱问个不停的嘴都安静了下来。
母亲常说，真正让人放心的，不只是他是军人，而是他做每件事都一直很认真。

example_translations.translation: That old serviceman at the station always spoke very slowly, but the moment he mentioned the friends who had gone through those years with him in youth, a bright light still came into his eyes.
When the child saw a soldier in neat uniform up close for the first time, even the mouth that usually loved asking endless questions fell quiet.
Mother often says that what truly makes a person reassuring is not only that he is a soldier, but that he does everything with real seriousness.

glosses.notes: Spread or distributed evenly, without some parts being much more or less than others.

examples.sentence: 母亲让孩子把盐撒得均匀一点，不然有的地方太淡，有的地方又一下重得让人吃不下。
这面墙的颜色看着很均匀，所以第一次来的人都看不出来它其实上个月才刚换过颜色。
老师提醒我们写字的时候别一会儿大一会儿小，先把每一行放得更均匀，看起来就会舒服很多。

example_translations.translation: Mother told the child to sprinkle the salt more evenly, otherwise some places would be too bland while others would suddenly be so strong that people could not eat it.
The color of this wall looks very even, so people coming for the first time cannot tell that its color was only changed last month.
The teacher reminded us not to make our writing big one moment and small the next. If we first make each line more even, it will look much more comfortable.

glosses.notes: A small card for information, identification, notes, or greetings.

examples.sentence: 孩子在那张小卡片上写完名字以后，又认真看了好几遍，怕自己一急就把最重要的字写错。
医生让她把那张卡片一直放在包里，因为上面写着药怎么吃、什么时候回来再看。
桌子上放着一堆旧卡片，看着不大，但是父亲一张一张地看过去，很快就想起以前的人和事。

example_translations.translation: After the child finished writing his name on that small card, he looked at it carefully several more times, afraid that in a rush he might have written the most important character wrong.
The doctor told her to keep that card in her bag at all times, because it said how to take the medicine and when to come back for another visit.
A pile of old cards was sitting on the table. It did not look like much, but as Father went through them one by one, he quickly remembered people and events from earlier years.

glosses.notes: To open up or create something new, especially a new method, road, or stage.

examples.sentence: 老人常说，前人开创这条路的时候没有今天这么好的条件，所以现在的人更不能随便说难。
那位老师后来能开创出自己的做法，不是因为他比别人快，而是因为他一直肯慢慢改。
父亲年轻时最佩服的，就是那些敢在没人试过的地方开创新办法的人，因为第一步总最难。

example_translations.translation: The old man often says that when the earlier generation opened up this road, they did not have conditions as good as today's, so people now should be even less ready to say something is too hard.
That teacher was later able to create his own method not because he was faster than others, but because he was always willing to make changes slowly.
What Father admired most in his youth were the people who dared to create new methods in places no one had tried before, because the first step is always the hardest.

glosses.notes: A switch or control used to turn something on or off.

examples.sentence: 孩子半夜起来找水时摸了半天，才找到旁边的开关，灯一亮，他先看见的还是前面那本书。
老房子的门边有两个开关，第一次来的人常常按错，所以父亲后来干脆在上面贴了小纸。
医生走以前提醒他，机器上的开关别让孩子乱碰，不然一按下去，前面白做的就都乱了。

example_translations.translation: When the child got up in the middle of the night to look for water, he felt around for quite a while before finding the switch beside him. As soon as the light came on, the first thing he saw was still the book in front of him.
There are two switches by the door of the old house, and people coming for the first time often press the wrong one, so later Father simply stuck small labels on them.
Before leaving, the doctor reminded him not to let the child touch the switch on the machine, because once it was pressed, all the work from before would be thrown into confusion.

glosses.notes: To open or start something, physically or in a more extended sense.

examples.sentence: 父亲轻轻一按，门就自动开启了，孩子站在边上看了半天，还以为里面有人在帮他们开。
机器一开启，原来一直很安静的大家都一起往前看，因为谁都想知道它这次会不会又停下来。
老师说，真正难的不是开启这件事，而是开启以后每天都还得继续做下去。

example_translations.translation: Father pressed lightly, and the door opened automatically. The child stood to the side watching for a long time, still thinking that someone inside was helping them open it.
As soon as the machine started up, the people who had been very quiet all looked forward together, because everyone wanted to know whether it would stop again this time.
The teacher said that the truly hard part is not opening something up, but continuing to do it every day after it has been opened.

glosses.notes: To open or establish a course, office, school, shop, or other organized offering.

examples.sentence: 学校今年新开设的那门课原来没人太注意，但是上了几次以后，连最不爱说话的孩子都开始回答了。
医院后来在楼下开设了一个小窗口，老人不用再跑到上面去问来问去，大家都觉得省了很多力。
他们想再开设一个小班，让住得远的孩子也能过来学，这样家里来回也会方便很多。

example_translations.translation: At first hardly anyone paid attention to the new course the school opened this year, but after a few sessions even the children who disliked speaking most started answering.
The hospital later set up a small window downstairs, so the old people no longer had to keep running upstairs to ask questions, and everyone felt it saved a lot of effort.
They want to open another small class so that children who live far away can also come study, and that would make things much more convenient for families going back and forth.

glosses.notes: The beginning of something, or the act of starting it.

examples.sentence: 这篇文章的开头看着很平，但是后面越看越精彩，所以孩子一坐下就一直看到很晚。
父亲讲话总爱先拿一件小事开头，因为这样大家比较容易听进去，后面再难的话也能慢慢说明白。
电影一开头就下大雨，连原来还在找位子的人都一下安静下来，想看后面到底会怎么走。

example_translations.translation: The beginning of this article looks plain, but the farther you read, the more exciting it becomes, so once the child sat down he kept reading until very late.
Father always likes to start with a small matter when speaking, because that way people find it easier to listen, and even harder things later can be explained slowly and clearly.
The film opens with heavy rain, and even the people who had still been looking for their seats suddenly quiet down because they want to see where it will go next.

glosses.notes: To chop or cut forcefully, or in some contexts to cut something down sharply.

examples.sentence: 父亲把门边长出来的旧树枝一点一点砍短，怕下一次风一大，它又打到窗上让人睡不着。
那块木头太大，他一个人砍了半天还是没有开，只好坐下来先喝口水，再慢慢接着做。
老人说，价格可以慢慢谈，但是如果别人一开口就乱砍太多，那这事反而更不容易说下去。

example_translations.translation: Father chopped the old branch by the door shorter bit by bit, afraid that when the wind grew strong next time it would hit the window again and keep people from sleeping.
That piece of wood was too large. He chopped at it for a long time by himself and still could not split it open, so he had to sit down, drink some water first, and then continue slowly.
The old man said that the price can be discussed slowly, but if the other side starts by slashing it down too much, the matter actually becomes harder to keep discussing.

glosses.notes: To look down on someone or treat them as not worthy of respect.

examples.sentence: 父亲一直提醒孩子，别因为别人做的事小就看不起人，因为真到难的时候，最先帮你的往往就是这些人。
她年轻时最怕别人看不起自己，所以哪怕再累，也总想把手里的事先做得像样一点。

examples.meaning_en: do not look down on yourself
examples.sentence: 老人常说，一个人最不该做的就是看不起自己，不然别人还没说什么，心里先已经站不起来了。

example_translations.translation: Father keeps reminding the child not to look down on people just because their work seems small, because when real difficulty comes, those very people are often the first to help you.
When she was young, what she feared most was other people looking down on her, so no matter how tired she was, she always wanted to do the work in her hands properly first.
The old man often says that the last thing a person should do is look down on himself, because then before anyone else has even said anything, his heart has already lost the strength to stand up.

glosses.notes: To regard, view, or treat something in a certain way.

examples.sentence: 老师让我们别只从输赢来看待这件事，因为真正重要的，往往是中间那段人怎么一起走过来。
父亲后来才明白，年纪一变，人看待很多老问题的办法也会和年轻时完全不一样。
医生说，别把一时的不舒服看待得太可怕，先看看身体后面几天到底怎么变，再慢慢决定。

example_translations.translation: The teacher told us not to regard this matter only in terms of winning and losing, because what is truly important is often how people made their way through the middle part together.
Only later did Father understand that once age changes, the way a person views many old problems can also become completely different from what it was in youth.
The doctor said not to treat a moment of discomfort as something too frightening. First watch how the body changes over the next few days, and then decide slowly.

glosses.notes: To think highly of someone, respect them, or feel they are worthy.

examples.sentence: 他虽然话不多，但是做事一直很认真，所以大家都看得起他，连要求最高的人也愿意把难事先交给他。
父亲常说，一个人先得自己看得起自己，不然别人就算给你机会，你也不一定敢接住。
老板后来一直看得起那个年轻人，不是因为他说得好听，而是因为他每次答应的事都真做到了。

example_translations.translation: Although he does not say much, he works very seriously, so everyone thinks highly of him, and even the people with the highest standards are willing to hand difficult tasks to him first.
Father often says that a person must first think highly of himself, because even if others give you a chance, you may still not dare to take it.
The boss later continued to think highly of that young man, not because he spoke pleasantly, but because every time he promised something, he truly followed through.

glosses.notes: To be optimistic about someone or something, or to think it has strong promise.

examples.sentence: 老师一直很看好这个孩子，因为他不是只在老师看着的时候才认真，而是平时也一直肯自己往前学。

examples.meaning_en: be optimistic about a new route
examples.sentence: 很多人都看好这条新路，因为一开通，原来要走很久的人以后出门就会方便很多。
母亲买东西以前先看了好几家，最后还是看好这家店，因为人虽然不多，但是东西一直很好。

example_translations.translation: The teacher has always been optimistic about this child, because he does not work seriously only when the teacher is watching; in ordinary times he is also always willing to keep learning on his own.
Many people are optimistic about this new route, because once it opens, people who used to spend a long time traveling will find it much more convenient to go out.
Before buying something, Mother looked at several places first, but in the end she still favored this shop, because although it is not crowded, the things there are always good.

glosses.notes: To seem or appear one way on the surface, especially when the reality may be different.

examples.sentence: 这道题看似很简单，但是真要一步一步写出来的时候，很多人还是会突然忘了中间怎么写。
这件事看似已经过去了，但是父亲一提起来，还是和那年一样难过。
那位老人看似总在笑，但是孩子和他坐久了才发现，他心里其实一直有很多没有说的话。

example_translations.translation: This problem seems very simple, but when people really have to write it out step by step, many still suddenly forget how the middle part should be written.
This matter seems to have already passed, but whenever Father brings it up, he is still just as sad as he was that year.
That old man always seems to be smiling, but after the child sat with him for a long time, he realized that the man still had many unspoken words in his heart.

glosses.notes: To take a liking to something or someone and choose it or them.

examples.sentence: 母亲看到那件外套以后，一下就看中它了，但是还是先把别的几家看完，怕自己一急又买得太早。
老板后来会看中他，不是因为他说得多好，而是因为最忙的时候他也一直没有先走。

examples.meaning_en: take a liking to a photo
examples.sentence: 孩子看中那张旧照片以后，一连问了很多次里面的人是谁，父亲只好坐下来慢慢讲。

example_translations.translation: After Mother saw that coat, she immediately took a fancy to it, but she still finished looking through several other places first, afraid that in a rush she might buy too early again.
The boss later chose him not because he spoke especially well, but because even at the busiest times he never slipped away first.
After the child took a fancy to that old photo, he kept asking who the people in it were, so Father had no choice but to sit down and explain slowly.

glosses.notes: To value something highly or regard it as especially important.

examples.sentence: 父亲一直很看重信用，所以哪怕只是和熟人说好的小事，他也一定会按时做完。
医生说，真正看重身体的人，不会只等到难受的时候才想起来要早点休息。
这家店看重的不是东西卖得多快，而是人下次还愿不愿意再回来，所以做得一直很认真。

example_translations.translation: Father has always valued trustworthiness very highly, so even if it is only a small matter agreed on with an acquaintance, he will still finish it on time.
The doctor says that people who truly value their health do not wait until they feel bad before remembering that they should rest earlier.
What this shop values is not how quickly things are sold, but whether people are willing to come back next time, so everything is done very carefully.

glosses.notes: To recover from illness, injury, or another physical setback.

examples.sentence: 医生说，他现在最重要的不是着急回去上班，而是先把身体慢慢康复好，不然前面的苦就白吃了。
孩子做完手术以后每天都认真走一会儿路，因为大家都知道，康复这件事急也急不来。
母亲看见他终于一点一点康复起来的时候，晚上回家连饭都比前一段多吃了一些。

example_translations.translation: The doctor said that the most important thing for him right now was not rushing back to work, but first slowly helping his body recover properly, otherwise all the hardship from before would have been for nothing.
After the child had surgery, he walked seriously for a little while every day, because everyone knew that recovery is something that cannot be rushed no matter how badly one wants to.
When Mother saw that he was finally recovering little by little, she even ate more that evening after going home than she had during the previous period.

glosses.notes: To investigate or inspect a place, situation, or method by looking at it carefully on site.

examples.sentence: 负责人这次去外地考察，不是只想看看新房子有多大，而是想知道别人到底怎么把后面的事安排好的。
老师让我们先考察一下这边的路和人，再决定活动那天从哪边走会更方便。
公司后来又派了两个人过去考察，因为第一次回来的人都说，那边真正难的地方还没有全看清。

example_translations.translation: This time the person in charge went elsewhere to inspect the situation not merely to see how large the new building was, but to understand how other people had arranged the later work well.
The teacher told us to first inspect the roads and the people on this side, and only then decide which way would be more convenient on the day of the activity.

The company later sent two more people there to inspect the situation again, because the people who came back the first time all said that the truly difficult parts there had still not been fully understood.
